instantiated_cells.justification: The definition of “lobbyist” includes any individual who “contracts for or receives economic consideration, other than reimbursement for actual expenses,” with no dollar minimum stated, so the compensation threshold is effectively $0.

A principal must register only after expenditures/obligations for nonexempt lobbying exceed $500 in a calendar year, and principals anticipating not exceeding $500 may file a verified statement and be exempt from licensing/registration/reporting if true.

unscoreable_emissions.reason: The bundled text defines “lobbyist” based on being employed/receiving economic consideration and a 5-days-in-period activity test, but it does not include any lobbyist-side expenditure amount that triggers registration.

Under the bundled sections, principals (not lobbyists) file expense statements, and while § 13.68 specifies certain thresholds (e.g., $200 per lobbyist; $500 grassroots ads), it does not impose a lobbyist-specific itemization/expenditure-reporting threshold.

The statute provides a 5-days-per-reporting-period test and a 10-hours-per-reporting-period exclusion for certain non-lobbyist employees in principals’ expense statements, but it does not create a lobbyist filing exemption based on a percentage of compensated time devoted to lobbying.
